gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-piazzolla: Expressive from the first glance, Bruno Ace draws its letters with a ruler-straight, constant-width line. Piazzolla takes over with a text serif whose lowercase nearly matches the capitals, giving the heading its showiness and the body its authority.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-pridi: Bruno Ace draws every stroke at a constant width, crossbars included, so the headline looks plotted with a ruler. Pridi softens that with a text serif of proud, almost capital-sized small letters and generous gaps where curves leave the stem.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-scope-one: Scope One has stubby ascenders and descenders beneath a big x-height, and its counters spill out into the space around them. Bruno Ace, meanwhile, offers a constant-width outline you could trace with a finger, which makes it the one built to catch attention.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-slabo-13px: Bruno Ace lets its counters stay connected to the outside, one character per lingering beat. Slabo 13px follows with a classic serif that has big open counters in a, e and s, so paragraphs would read in a dignified, bookish way.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-suwannaphum: Bruno Ace has no thick-and-thin contrast to slow the eye. Suwannaphum answers with a tall, squared-off lowercase and a wide-open c, and that gap between low-key heading and high-reaching body is what the pair does best.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-epunda-slab: Bruno Ace SC spreads its letters like beads on a thread. Next to it, Epunda Slab brings tall rounded lowercase and a visibly gaping c, so the strongest quality here is a heading with constant stroke weight set against a dignified classic serif.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-fauna-one: Beaded, wide-set letters with zero sparkle. Fauna One steps in with a literary serif, its tall middle band and shallow ascenders and descenders giving the pair a strongest quality of display flair set against quiet, dignified text.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-glegoo: Bruno Ace SC strings its open-aperture letters out with the steadiness of a drawn string, and nothing in it thins or swells. Glegoo's big counters and wide curved mouths keep long text open.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-hanuman: Bruno Ace SC has no swelling where its curves meet the stems, which gives each letter a drawn, uniform feel. And Hanuman, a text serif with a high-waisted lowercase and wide-set terminals on s, stays traditional beneath it, while the heading earns its keep big and short.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-kadwa: Bruno Ace SC spreads out its letters with no calligraphic swell on any downstroke. Kadwa, a serif with open-ended curves and a larger-than-usual x-height, brings the classic editorial warmth, and that difference is the strongest thing about the pair.
